title: The AI race has stopped being company vs. company — it's now nation vs. nation
explanation: The same week China released the largest open-weights model ever built, 29 countries launched a new AI governance body in Shanghai with no Western democracies present. These aren't two separate stories. They're the same story: the contest for who sets the terms of AI — technically, legally, diplomatically — has shifted from competing labs to competing blocs.

evidence.text: Kimi K3, released with open weights at 2.8 trillion parameters, halted new subscriptions within 48 hours — global demand overwhelmed capacity before any regulatory response could form. The model runs on servers worldwide, including in WAICO member nations. It is the largest open-weights model ever released, larger than anything currently available from Western labs.
WAICO, a new AI coordination body, launched in Shanghai with 29 member nations. Not a single Western democracy is among them.

The White House's distillation claim put Anthropic in an unusual position: the company whose model was allegedly used to build Kimi K3 is now on record saying it does not support a ban on open-weight models. Dario Amodei, posting July 27, called non-dangerous open models 'a public good' while backing anti-distillation enforcement and chip export controls — a middle position that left Anthropic as the only major US lab not on the Nvidia-led open letter. The victim of alleged IP theft is now defining the distinction between 'open weights' (acceptable) and 'distillation' (not) — a legal category that doesn't fully exist yet.
